items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: I started out with a band in Miami when I was fourteen years old, called George Kelly and the Cavaliers. And I was with them until I was eighteen

ctx.x: Tell us some of the big bands that you played with. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

Well I started out with a band in Miami when I was fourteen years old, called George Kelly and the Cavaliers. And I was with them until I was eighteen, and I went to Tampa to join a band that was fronted by a guy named Charlie Brantley. And then I left and went to New York. And I did something in New York that very few musicians or very few people in show business have done. I got to New York on a Tuesday and went to work Sunday and I never looked back. I was like one of the first ones of my peers to leave home.…
Tell us about how it was like, the travel, the pay, the lifestyle of working with the traveling band.

items.q: Yeah, the George Kelly we know, in a local band -- a bunch of teenaged kids. Teenagers. But they had this little band, George Kelly and his Cavaliers.
